title: Wolf's Family Home
text: “So this is Wolf-san’s estate?”
“Theo’s family home was pretty big too, but this place is something else, huh.”
“It feels more like a castle, doesn’t it?”
Indeed, where we had arrived was… a castle-ish estate on par with the hotels on Cal Mira Island, I say. It was a bit smaller, but it definitely looked like a castle.
“Guess Wolf’s family really is a big deal.”
“Old bloodline. Decent battle record generation after generation, so reputation domestically is high. Different faction from Four Great Tribes, but cooperate sometimes.”
“Huh.”
“Though lately, everyone besides my brother’s been kind of pathetic, and truth is we’ve had money troubles. Repairs haven’t kept up.”
“So even a flashy house has its dirty laundry, huh.”
“Woof. Been managing that side of things.”
As Wolf said this and started unloading the luggage, a swarm of servants came pouring out of the castle.
“Magarum-sama, welcome home!”
A wolfman butler, apparently the representative of the servants, gave a sharp salute.
“Shield Hero-sama! Welcome, welcome!”
“Yeah. Going to be in your care for a while.”
“Yes!”
“So, Wolf. Where are your parents?”
“Woof— read the room and had them go out this time.”
“Had them go out?”
Father tilted his head. Why arrange for them not to be here, I wondered.
“Heh.”
Wolf let out an ominous little laugh, putting on a sharp expression that clearly said she had no intention of explaining further.
“Guess that means it’d be a problem if we saw them?” Rabbit Guy said, pushing up his glasses in a competing gesture.
“You mean they’re weird parents?”
“Fufu.”
“Why so mysterious about it? I wanted to say hello.”
“Sounds like the type of parents you’d be in trouble for seeing. Iwatani-sama, you should be careful about how close you get with Wolf on this topic.”
“Is that how it is? Oh? Wait, are they carrying something?”

Father’s eyes drifted toward some servants who seemed to be in the middle of moving something out—people carrying what looked like a framed picture. Wolf swiftly cut across to block Father’s view. I caught a glimpse of it, though, I say. It looked like a portrait of some wolfman family. I could tell it was Wolf in demi-human form, presumably as a child, along with someone who must have been her brother. I’d never actually met him, but I recalled seeing Takt’s fox in transformed shape once, and there was a certain resemblance lingering about him. As for the parents… there was one wolfman, and what looked like another rather manly figure. Was that the mother? Or, wait, was the wolfman female? The muscular one had looked male to me, but I honestly couldn’t tell. When Wolf shot a glance their way, the servants scrambled to flip the painting face-down and hauled it off as though fleeing the scene.
“Since guests were coming, had redecorating ordered—place looked too old-fashioned.”
“You didn’t have to worry about that.”
“Don’t want to be called gloomy. Want the family to properly show authority too. Parents still bearable, but the troublesome ones got removed. Woof!”
“Guess that’s just how it is. Well, Wolf was apparently the brains of the operation back here, so I’ll leave the judgment calls to you.”
“Let’s get moving already.”

Crocodile Guy, sighing faintly, entered the castle with luggage in hand… and on the wall hung an old painting: a figure holding a shield, presumably a past Shield Hero, alongside a wolfman, a lizardman resembling Crocodile Guy, and… some kind of weasel-like beastman, all rendered in an aged portrait. Thanks to what looked like traces of restoration work, the Shield Hero’s face was impossible to make out, I say. Crocodile Guy’s gaze fixed on the painting.

“That painting’s said to be one of the restorations of the original Shield Hero and his companions. But a lot of records were lost, so no telling if it’s accurate. Was in the back of the storeroom here—brought it out for this occasion.”
“…I see.”
Crocodile Guy studied the painting closely. His expression looked almost nostalgic.
“Guess we’ll eventually go see the place that’s the roots of Shion too?”
“No, my father was the last of his line. Nothing should be left at that place. Pretty much no point going.”
“I see.”
“Besides, Seaetto’s basically like my hometown now, so no need to worry about it.”
“Got it.”
“Let’s hurry and get the luggage to the rooms.”

At Wolf’s suggestion, Crocodile Guy obediently carried the bags onward. So this was Wolf’s family home. I had memories of pigs living in castles like this too, come to think of it. Well, I was pretty used to the sight of Melromarc’s castle and the like, so I didn’t have much of a reaction.
“Welcome, welcome! Shield Hero-sama!”
And so, with the servants once again putting on a show of hospitality, we were guided toward the residential wing.

“Ah, this is going to be tough for me to enter,” Elephant said, faltering at the sheer size of the building. By wolfman standards, each doorway was larger than in an ordinary castle, but it still seemed a bit much for Elephant to fit through. Crouching down, it looked like she might just manage it—though she’d have to stay half-bent the whole way.
“Woof, there’s a section for guests. Tall beastmen fine over there.”
Wolf pointed the way.
“Would it be alright if I stayed over there instead? …Since I’ve technically been assigned to guard duty.”
“Can eat meals together in the plaza and such. That should work fine. Won’t let any indecent types anywhere near here, so no worries.”
With a sharp, commanding expression, Wolf gave the order, and the servants nodded while saluting.
“Understood. We’ll arrange it in a suitable style for receiving guests.”
“Mm. Please do.”
The servants sprang into brisk, efficient motion, each hurrying off to their tasks.
“Heh… Wolf’s really got the whole head-of-household thing down, huh.”
“Technically, thanks to title of Claw Hero, authority’s highest now. Brother’s pretty laid-back about this stuff, and I’ve been managing in his place for a while, so used to it.”
“Guess that’s how it goes.”
“Rebellious factions already driven out, so no worries. Please, relax without concern.”
“Got it, but… come to think of it, since this is your territory, Wolf, we did pass through some villages on the way.”
Father had been observing things along the road. He’d been asking all sorts of questions.
“Is it okay to be away? Seems like there’d be a mountain of paperwork waiting.”
“Fine. Already sent instructions based on documents that came in to the Siltvelt castle.”

She answered as though paperwork were her forte… though I couldn’t help but suspect she might be avoiding reality by comparison to the mountains of documents someone like Éclair dealt with. Was she really as reliable as she made out?
“Guess that much is fine, then. Oh, speaking of which… there were quite a lot of humans in the villages around here. Are they slaves?”
“Woof, no… but status is low.”
“Siltvelt really does vary a lot by region, doesn’t it,” Rabbit Guy chimed into the conversation there. That was true, I supposed.
“Around Elephant’s family home, there are plenty of human slaves, I say.”

Or rather, since the mammoth folk of Elephant’s household were too massive to handle all the fiddly little tasks around their territory, their policy seemed to be bringing in humans for exactly that kind of labor.
“It’s an embarrassing topic.”
“Planning to visit there too, at some point.”
“I’d rather you didn’t.”
“Fear not, Elephant! It will surely go well, indeed. The loyalty of Mouse is absolute!”
“What are you even talking about…”
“Heheh… Elmeloooo. I sure would love to visit your family home… seeing as I let all sorts of squatters move into mine while I wasn’t around.”
Panda taunted Elephant with a resentful look.
“Larsa… haah, there was no stopping it, not with the way things went.”
“Mouse, um… the Puhant family charged in recklessly and challenged Janon over and over, only to get thrashed every time.”
“Ah, right… wasn’t that Elmelo-san’s adoptive parent or something?”
Wolf seemed to know something about this.

“Heard about it through rumors. After the war started by the Hakuko king ended in crushing defeat against Melromarc’s Wise Sage King, there was internal strife within Siltvelt, and apparently their pride got wounded. Went invading the territory hoping to restore face and grab some labor, and got thoroughly beaten back.”
“…Heard Janon-sama utterly wrecked them.”
Elephant broke into a wicked grin rarely seen on her, jeering at the mammoths. Well, they were foolish mammoths, after all.
